text:
The Maple Leafs have gone eight straight without a win (0-7-1), outscored 33-15, and this one isn't a goaltending story or a bad-bounce story. They have 43% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in that run. Thursday's loss to Los Angeles, a three-goal lead turned into a shootout defeat, is the kind that sticks to a dressing room. The noise around it is enormous: 30 headlines each in two weeks for Auston Matthews, William Nylander, Gavin McKenna and Morgan Rielly, with the Matthews trade chatter now including a report that the Flyers have called. Jim Hiller is scratching Oliver Ekman-Larsson tonight, per the beat, and Anthony Stolarz starts.

Our numbers give Toronto a 2.4% playoff chance. That figure would have read as a typo in October.

Columbus walks in with its own problems, just quieter ones. The 4-2 win in Chicago ended a five-game winless run, and the Blue Jackets sit at 7% to make it. Zach Werenski's name has started showing up in trade buzz, which says something about how this season has gone. Sean Monahan (upper body) is out, Conor Garland is on injured reserve, and Adam Fantilli has moved beside Valeri Nichushkin. Cam Talbot has been better than anyone expected, nearly six goals saved above expected after minus 13.7 last season.

Then there's the reunion. Matthew Knies plays in Toronto for the first time since the trade, after 240 games as a Leaf, and Steven Lorentz comes back with him. Knies says the return "feels a little awkward," per the beat, and he had a big night in Chicago on the way in. Our numbers lean Columbus, 3.33 expected goals to 2.92, with Mathieu Olivier (20% to score, one goal from 50 for his career) and Toronto's Easton Cowan, up to about 19 minutes a night, as our sleepers.
headline: Eight without a win, and Knies comes home
